title: Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor Levels in Dependence and Withdrawal Phases of Morphine Addiction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Rodent Studies
abstract: Abstract Introduction Morphine addiction is a chronic relapsing disorder associated with numerous molecular alterations in different brain regions. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), a member of the neurotrophin family of growth factors that plays differential roles in various brain areas, is involved in morphine addiction. However, no comprehensive synthesis has been conducted to compare BDNF expression across brain regions and during different morphine addiction phases. Methods This systematic search of electronic databases yielded 44 original peer-reviewed studies using the keywords “morphine” and “BDNF.” Relevant data were extracted from the included studies. The risk of bias was assessed using the Systematic Review Centre for Laboratory animal Experimentation (SYRCLE)’s risk bias tool. Study characteristics were summarised, risks of bias were reported, and a meta-analysis was conducted. Heterogeneity and publication bias were also evaluated. Results After repeated morphine exposure, BDNF levels differed during the dependence and withdrawal phases, as well as across various brain regions, including the ventral tegmental area, striatum, and frontal cortex. Conclusion These results highlight the potential of BDNF as a biomarker for morphine addiction and may contribute to improved interventions and outcomes for individuals with morphine addiction. However, further studies are warranted to explore these neurobiological processes before altering BDNF levels to treat morphine addiction.
